target_customer: Developers and companies building video into their products
problem: Developers need video analytics and streaming infrastructure without building encoding, delivery and quality monitoring themselves.
business_model: Usage-based API for video streaming and analytics

founders.name: Adam Brown
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked at companies building large scale video streaming, transcoding and 3D rendering cloud systems.

founders.name: Steve Heffernan
previous_startups: Zencoder (YC W10, acquired by Brightcove in 2012)

founders.name: Matthew McClure
founders.role: Co-founder, Head of Technology and Community
founders.background_notes: YC page says core contributor to Video.js and organizer of the Demuxed conference.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video analytics at scale and later encoding, storage and delivery require deep media engineering; the founders had built Zencoder and Video.js before.

defensibility.rationale: Developer integrations and data create stickiness, but large cloud vendors and CDNs offer substitutes; the team's reputation helped distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought Mux; it grew independently, did its first acquisition (Stream Club) in December 2021, and laid off about 20 percent of staff in October 2022.

market_need_then: Contrary Research says the team led with a data product because established video API competitors had large engineering capacity. Mux's own April 2017 post says video was exploding, and the 2016 seed press framed quality control of video as an unmet need.

branding.name_origin: Several sources tie the name to multiplexing, combining signals into one; the company sources are not a founder statement of the choice.

identity.logo: Identity redone by agency For The People, inspired by Erector sets with slider toggles
identity.visual_style: Square-countered grotesk with black, neon and signal green palette

branding.brand_signature: Demuxed, the video engineers conference the founders organize, a wordplay on the company name

rebrands.why: Not stated; the It's Nice That article is dated May 2023 by URL.

branding.community_and_virality: Founders run Demuxed, a conference for video engineers, and Video.js community ties exist; no merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer community through Video.js and Demuxed plus a distinctive short name and a design agency refresh show brand investment and reputation among video developers.

pivots.to: Added Mux Video, a video streaming API
pivots.why: Contrary Research says analytics came first because established video API competitors existed; Mux announced Mux Video in November 2017.

outcome_analysis: Mux was founded by the creators of Zencoder and Video.js and raised five rounds from a 2.8 million seed in 2016 to a 105 million Series D in April 2021, which press reported at over one billion dollars. It added a video API in 2017 after starting with analytics. Growth slowed after the 2021 peak with a 20 percent layoff in October 2022, yet it remains active and signed Synthesia in 2025.
notes: Series D valuation was reported as over 1 billion dollars without an exact figure, so post_money is null. Series B date is 2019 per VentureBeat summary; month not seen. Mux's own site fetch was rate limited once and succeeded on a single retry. Series A 9 million brought total to 12 million including seed per Mux's post; Series D total 175 million (pulse2). Competitors dated near the batch were not found: sources describe established players generally without names and dates, so the list is empty. Rebrand year comes from the article URL and is low confidence.
